title: SoPPIs: a highly parallelized protein-protein-interaction screening method in prokaryotic and eukaryotic hosts.
data_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13389306/supplementaryFiles (Datasets 1-3, .xlsx); raw reads: ENA PRJEB76943; analysis notebooks: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.29236658

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the 11.4 MB supplement and opened all three Excel files. Dataset 1: 11,018 bait-prey rows over 25 bait sheets, 3,462 unique Arabidopsis gene IDs (AGI codes like AT1G01010), columns ID / FS / FS(0-1) / MS for each of two biological replicates, no missing values. Dataset 3: exactly 3,213 rows, 2,034 unique prey genes, only 17 baits, and two baits (LSM7 1,159 rows, LSM4 1,063 rows) supply 69% of all pairs. Replicate agreement of the score MS in Dataset 3 is Spearman 0.22 (Pearson of log10 values 0.20, median absolute log10 replicate ratio 0.36). Dataset 2: all 625 pairs of the 25x25 LSm/Sm matrix, of which 540 (86%) score above zero; the PCR-free and PCR-based protocols agree at Spearman 0.953, but agreement with STRING (a public interaction database) combined score is only Spearman 0.25. I also read the supplementary PDF (20 pages): Table S1 is the 25 bait gene IDs, Table S2 is a list of raw FASTQ filenames. The figshare record is 122 KB of Jupyter notebooks (software only, CC BY 4.0), no data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Definitions of the scores (FS = observed frequency / expected frequency; FS(0-1) rescaled; MS median-normalized significance score), the claim that ~400,000 bait-prey combinations were screened from a 15,175-gene cDNA library, and the statement that only 799 of the 3,462 recovered interactors were in frame with the N-terminal Cre tag. I did not download the raw sequencing reads from ENA (raw FASTQ is out of scope and the project rules forbid it).

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement zip and all three Excel datasets downloaded and opened with no login; notebooks on figshare are CC BY 4.0. Raw reads are openly in ENA PRJEB76943.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. Interaction scores exist only for pairs the assay detected; there is no non-interacting class anywhere in the files. The cDNA library gene list and per-gene abundances (needed to define 'tested but not detected') are not supplied in any table, so negatives would have to be reconstructed from raw FASTQ in ENA. The only all-by-all table (625 LSm/Sm pairs) is 86% positive among 25 proteins of one family, so it supplies almost no negatives either.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL in practice. Only gene identifiers are given, so protein sequences need one bulk Araport11 download (cheap). But the prey is a random cDNA fragment of unknown length and reading frame: the paper states only 799 of 3,462 interactors were in frame with the Cre tag, and no frame or fragment-boundary column exists in the files, so the polypeptide actually assayed is unknown for most rows.

a4_units_stated.note: FS, FS(0-1) and MS are dimensionless ratios with definitions given in Methods and Supplementary Fig. S6; column headers in all three Excel files are consistent.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL as 'enough rows in disguise'. 11,018 pairs (3,213 high-confidence) look sufficient, but the independent unit is the bait: 25 baits, 17 with any high-confidence hit, and LSM7 plus LSM4 alone give 69% of pairs; six baits have 6 or fewer. All 25 baits are members of one protein family (Sm-fold spliceosome ring), so held-out-bait evaluation has ~2 informative groups.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 11.4 MB supplement (three Excel files, 1.4 MB of data)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; only the ENA raw reads would be large, and I did not fetch them.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Exact match: files give 11,018 pairs / 3,462 proteins (paper: 11,018 / 3,462) and 3,213 pairs / 2,034 proteins (paper: 3,213 / 2,034), and 625 pairs for the 25x25 matrix.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels come from a physical measurement (counting sequencing reads of recombined plasmids), normalized by plasmid-pool abundance, not from another model's prediction. The concern is noise, not circularity: replicate Spearman is 0.22 on the authors' own high-confidence subset.

existing_models.name: PLM-interact (2025, Nature Communications) - fine-tunes ESM-2, a protein language model, on pairs of interacting and non-interacting proteins
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported cross-species protein-protein interaction gains over earlier models; exact numbers not retrieved beyond the search abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalization across species and to proteins unlike the training set.

existing_models.name: D-SCRIPT and Topsy-Turvy (2021-2022) - sequence-based deep models for physical protein interaction
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked cross-species; code and docs public (d-script.readthedocs.io). Numbers not retrieved in detail.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-species transfer and scarcity of reliable negative examples.

existing_models.name: TUnA (2024, Briefings in Bioinformatics) - uncertainty-aware transformer on ESM-2 embeddings
existing_models.score_and_split: Highest area under the precision-recall curve across five species versus Topsy-Turvy, per the paper abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Calibrated confidence for out-of-distribution protein pairs.

existing_models.name: DeepAraPPI / AraPPINet / PAIR - Arabidopsis-specific interaction predictors and predicted interactome resources
existing_models.score_and_split: AraPPINet reports >345,000 predicted Arabidopsis interactions; DeepAraPPI combines sequence, domain and Gene Ontology features. Splits not verified.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Sparse gold-standard plant interaction data and paralog expansion.

existing_models.name: Y2H-SCORES (PLOS Computational Biology) - statistical scoring of sequencing-based two-hybrid screens
existing_models.score_and_split: Ranks interactors by enrichment and specificity; applied to the barley MLA immune receptor screen.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Separating true interactors from abundance-driven background in next-generation two-hybrid data.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model, small CPU checkpoints)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for ~3,500 Arabidopsis proteins

integration.partner_dataset: STRING v12 and the Arabidopsis Splicing Related Genes (ASRG) database; the paper already ships a STRING sheet for the 625 LSm/Sm pairs
integration.join_key: Arabidopsis gene identifier (AGI code, e.g. AT1G01010) mapped to UniProt
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which sequencing-based interaction calls are supported by independent evidence rather than by transcript abundance - answerable in principle, but the screen supplies no negatives to train on and the quantitative score does not replicate.

controls.positive_control: The LSm/Sm ring members should recover each other; in the 625-pair matrix 540 pairs score above zero, so this control is uninformative (almost everything is positive).
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable but meaningless without a negative class.
controls.external_validation: STRING channel scores are provided for the 625 matrix pairs (agreement Spearman 0.25) and ASRG is named in the paper; no second independent SoPPIs dataset exists.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained on these files could only claim to predict how large a read-frequency score an Arabidopsis cDNA fragment received when co-expressed with one of two heavily sampled Sm-family baits in E. coli, among fragments the assay already detected - and since the two biological replicates of that score agree at Spearman 0.22, even that claim is mostly a claim about noise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequences to predict which Arabidopsis proteins bind spliceosome LSm/Sm ring proteins in a sequencing-based interaction screen.
plain_idea.train_on: Pairs of an LSm/Sm bait protein and an Arabidopsis prey protein, each represented by its amino acid sequence (fetched in bulk from the Araport11 annotation using the gene identifiers in the files). Verified counts: 11,018 detected pairs over 25 baits, or 3,213 high-confidence pairs over 17 baits.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the pair interacts, or how strong the interaction score is. The true answer comes from SoPPIs: two plasmids each carrying half of the Cre recombinase recombine only when the two proteins touch, and the recombined DNA is counted by high-throughput sequencing, giving a frequency score normalized to each gene's abundance in the plasmid pool.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant interaction-prediction models are trained on thin gold-standard data, so a genuinely new experimental screen of thousands of pairs would be valuable training and test material. As the data stands, the main thing learned is how irreproducible one such screen's quantitative scores are.

more_or_better_data.why: Existing Arabidopsis predictors train on tens of thousands of curated pairs (AraPPINet alone reports >345,000 predicted interactions built on curated positives); this paper adds 3,213-11,018 positives from one lab, one assay, one host, with 69% coming from two baits.

confidence_score.why: There are two biological replicates, which is the right ingredient for calibration, but their agreement on the high-confidence subset is Spearman 0.22, so replicate-based uncertainty would swamp the signal. TUnA (2024) already provides calibrated uncertainty for sequence-based interaction prediction.

models_beatable.why: The relevant comparators are recent and open: PLM-interact (2025), TUnA (2024), Topsy-Turvy (2022), all built on protein language models and evaluated across species. There is no published number on this dataset to beat, and no negative class to compute one.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on every condition: the new data measures interaction by a different assay in a different host than the curated positives those models use, there is no shared evaluation split, and no negative examples, so the existing models cannot even be scored on these rows.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a frozen ESM-2 embedding plus a small classifier head to predict LSm/Sm interaction partners from Arabidopsis protein sequence, using the 3,213 high-confidence SoPPIs pairs as positives, with held-out baits and sequence-identity-clustered preys. It dies on the missing negative class (the tested-but-not-detected set would have to be rebuilt from raw ENA reads), on bait imbalance (two baits give 69% of pairs, all 25 baits are one protein family), and on the label's own noise (replicate Spearman 0.22).

effort.compute_note: The supplied tables are tiny (1.4 MB of data) and parse in seconds, which I timed; the 40 hours is an estimate for the step that actually matters - reprocessing the ENA FASTQ files to recover the cDNA library composition and per-gene abundances needed to define negatives, which the project rules also forbid.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Correlate the two biological replicates of the MS score in Dataset 3 (one line of pandas): it is Spearman 0.22 on the authors' own high-confidence subset, so the quantitative label is not reproducible. Second check: count the negatives - there are none.

verdict_reason: Opened all three supplementary datasets; counts match the paper exactly (11,018 / 3,462 / 3,213 / 2,034 / 625), but the data fails three Part A killers. A2: only detected pairs are recorded, the cDNA library gene list is not supplied, so the non-interacting class would have to be rebuilt from raw sequencing reads, and the one all-by-all table is 86% positive among 25 proteins of a single family. A3: the prey is a random cDNA fragment of unknown frame (only 799 of 3,462 hits were in frame with the Cre tag) and no frame column exists, so the assayed polypeptide is unknown for most rows. A5 in disguise: the independent unit is the bait - 25 baits, 17 with hits, two of them supplying 69% of pairs. On top of that the quantitative label does not replicate (Spearman 0.22 between biological replicates) and the field is served by open, recent models (PLM-interact 2025, TUnA 2024, Topsy-Turvy 2022). This is an excellent methods paper whose shipped tables are a hit list, not a feature/label table.
